$comment: Which `workflows/99_e2e` fixtures this app implements, and which individual
tests its runtime cannot pass yet. Format and ratcheting rules:
Grow the list as fixtures are ported to `workflows/99_e2e.py`, one at a time,
and only once the test passes. Never shrink it without saying why.

unsupported.FatalError fails immediately without ret: The step lifecycle is right — `FatalError` burns exactly one attempt — but the run's `errorCode` is not. vercel-py writes `run_failed.code` as `type(e).__name__`, and by then the step's `FatalError` has been rehydrated into a `RuntimeError`, so the run carries `RuntimeError` where the test expects `USER_ERROR`.
unsupported.FatalError can be caught and detected wi: A thrown error does not keep its identity across the event log: vercel-py writes `step_failed.error` as text and the workflow side raises `RuntimeError(<text>)`, so the `FatalError` the step raised is no longer one by the time the body catches it. Upstream needs the serialized-error pipeline (`SerializedData` in place of the pre-#1851 `StructuredError` shape) before this and the two `RoundTrip` fixtures can pass.
unsupported.hookWithSleepWorkflow - hook payloads de: The run stalls on the first payload: `hook_created`, `wait_created` and `hook_received` are written, the `processPayload` step the body calls next never is — no `step_created`, no error, the delivery answers 200. `hookWithSleepFinalStepWorkflow` passes and takes the same hook twice before its one step, and `sleepWithSequentialStepsWorkflow` passes with the same never-completing `sleep('1d')` in front of three sequential steps, so neither the concurrent wait nor a step after a hook is enough on its own. What is left is the transition only this fixture makes: resuming from `hook_received` straight into a new step suspension. An observed shape, not a root cause.
unsupported.hookTokenReuseLoopWorkflow - same run re: The driver waits for a new `hookId` on the same token after each `dispose()`, and round 1 keeps seeing round 0's. vercel-py flushes `hook_created` and `hook_disposed` from one task group with no ordering between them, which is what upstream #2777 fixed on the TypeScript side: the disposal has to be flushed before the next creation is validated, or the run records a conflict against its own disposed hook.
unsupported.hookWithSleepFinalStepWorkflow - step on: Vercel world only, and the local lane passes it — but `unsupported` is not lane-aware, so the exemption costs that local signal. On Vercel the driver is an external resumer with no symmetric run key, so `@workflow/world-vercel` seals the hook payload to the run's public key in the X25519 `encp` format. vercel-py reads `encr` (#279) and not `encp`, so the run fails at the first payload with `SerializationError: ... uses the 'encp' format, which this SDK cannot read`, and the driver's second `resumeHook` then 404s with `HookNotFoundError`. This is the first fixture to make the suite produce an `encp` payload at all, and it applies to every hook fixture on that lane, not just this one.
unsupported.resilient start: addTenWorkflow complete: Was the missing run row; is now a defect one layer further in. The pinned rev carries vercel-py #282-#284, so the handler does bootstrap from `run_started` - and then dies validating the run it bootstrapped: `2 validation errors for NonFinalWorkflowRun / input.bytes / input.str - input_value={'__type': 'Uint8Array', ... 'ZGV2bFtbMV0sMTIzXQ=='}` (that base64 is `devl[[1],123]`, this fixture's own input). `RunInput.input` is typed `Any` (`world.py:117`), so the `Uint8Array` envelope the local world's JSON queue transport wraps `bytes` in is never decoded, and `NonFinalWorkflowRun.input` (`world.py:220`) wants `bytes | str`. Local world only - the Vercel world's CBOR transport carries bytes natively, and the stack's own unit tests use fakes with no transport at all.
